correctness.rationale: For a symmetric marginal with second moment \(s\) and quadratic variance \(h>0\), the univariate basis is \(1\), \(t/\sqrt{s}\), and \((t^2-s)/\sqrt h\). The total-degree-two product basis also contains all pair products of first-degree factors. Its kernel is equation (1) in RESULT.md. Parseval bounds the linear/diagonal remainder by \(O(\sqrt d)\) in expected absolute value. The cross-coordinate chaos is \(\big((\sum_i x_iY_i)^2-\sum_i x_i^2Y_i^2\big)/(2s^2)\). If \(q_d=d^{-1}\sum_i x_i^2\) tends to \(q>0\), bounded triangular-array Lindeberg and an \(L^2\) law of large numbers yield \(q(Z^2-1)/(2s)\) after division by dimension. A uniform second-moment bound yields convergence of absolute first moments, including the \(q=0\) case. A subsequence argument proves uniformity; endpoint support gives \(q=1\), and the positive sharp limit gives the extremizer equivalence. Gaussian integration by parts gives \(\mathbb E|Z^2-1|=4/\sqrt{2\pi e}\). The checker independently verifies exact finite polynomial-kernel Gram identities in dimensions one through four and finite stochastic trends, without using them to prove the limit.

originality.rationale: Bounded searches of the published mathematical record, the semantic research index, and previously published mathematical statements found no theorem implying the dimension-uniform quadratic product-projection Lebesgue profile or its corner rigidity. The closest published hypercube papers concern best approximation with changing polynomial degree (Trefethen 2016) or discrete hyperinterpolation in three dimensions (Caliari et al. 2008). Closest indexed quadratic Walsh, Hamming and Johnson spectral projections concern distinct discrete measures and operator domains, and their Gaussian constants alone do not imply the continuous product-marginal universality and support-localization conclusion. Previously published statements on weighted-ball degree two and cube affine projectors are not instances of the general symmetric product projector. Search is not proof of priority; see residual risks.
residual_risks: An older theorem on universal high-dimensional polynomial-chaos projection constants under an alternative title may imply the result; searches cannot exclude it.

value.rationale: The norm is a canonical sharp L∞ stability factor in multivariate quadratic least-squares approximation. The theorem specifies a universal full spatial profile for all symmetric compact product priors, demonstrates independence of the fourth moment (only the variance enters the sharp leading constant), and identifies exactly which evaluation sequences are asymptotically worst. These are substantive questions in fixed-degree/high-dimensional approximation and yield explicit Legendre, Chebyshev, Jacobi and mixed-measure coefficients not implied by the cited fixed-dimensional and/or high-degree analyses. No general downstream theorem is required for this motivated exact asymptotic invariant.
